name: Decision-Pretrained Transformer (DPT) — Supervised Pretraining Can Learn In-Context Reinforcement Learning
venue: NeurIPS 2023 (Thirty-seventh Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems). DBLP: conf/nips/0002XPCFNB23. Also arXiv:2306.14892 (cs.LG), submitted 26 Jun 2023.
authors_affiliation: Jonathan N. Lee (co-first), Annie Xie (co-first), Aldo Pacchiano, Yash Chandak, Chelsea Finn, Ofir Nachum, Emma Brunskill. Primary affiliation: Stanford University. The arXiv v1 lists Aldo Pacchiano at Microsoft Research and Ofir Nachum at Google DeepMind; the NeurIPS camera-ready instead lists Pacchiano at Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard / Boston University. Correspondence: jnl@stanford.edu, anniexie@stanford.edu.
code_url: https://github.com/jon--lee/decision-pretrained-transformer (official, Python/PyTorch, GPT-2 backbone via HuggingFace transformers)
maintained_repo_url: N/A (single-paper code repository, not a continuously-maintained leaderboard or paper list).
task_domain: Decision-making / reinforcement learning: in-context RL for multi-armed bandits (incl. linear bandits) and finite-horizon Markov Decision Processes (gridworld navigation 'Dark Room', image-based navigation 'Miniworld'). Embodied/control-flavored but the core contribution is a meta-RL / in-context-learning method for sequential decision-making, not language QA.
problem_setting: Meta-RL style in-context decision-making. A diverse distribution of tasks (bandits / MDPs) is available at pretraining; for each task an 'in-context dataset' D of (s,a,s',r) interaction tuples is sampled (random, expert, or algorithm-generated), a query state s_query is sampled, and an OPTIMAL action label a* (from the optimal policy of that task, or from an RL-trained agent when the optimum is unavailable) is the supervision target. A causal GPT-2 transformer M_theta is trained purely by supervised learning (negative log-likelihood / softmax classification) to predict a* given (s_query, D). At test time NO parameter updates occur: the frozen model is deployed as either an OFFLINE RL algorithm (argmax over actions conditioned on a fixed dataset D) or an ONLINE RL algorithm (sample actions, append the resulting interactions to D, repeat across episodes). Single-agent. Supervision (optimal-action labels) is required at pretraining; this is the key assumption and stated limitation.
what_is_retrieved: Not classical document/demo retrieval. The functional analog of 'retrieved context' is the in-context interaction dataset D = {(s_j, a_j, s'_j, r_j)} of transition tuples from the unknown current task, placed in the transformer's context window. There is no similarity search; D is supplied (offline) or accumulated online by the model's own rollouts. Pretraining additionally 'retrieves'/samples (query-state, optimal-action) supervision pairs, but at deployment the conditioning context is the task's own interaction history.
retrieval_grounding: Closest to a GROWING/episodic in-context store in the ONLINE setting (the in-context dataset D starts empty and is grown by the agent's own interactions across episodes), and a STATIC per-task dataset in the OFFLINE setting (a fixed prompt D ~ D_test). There is NO external static corpus / knowledge base / API store being searched; conditioning is on the agent's own task interactions. Best summarized as: in-context (test-time) interaction context, episodically grown online vs fixed offline — not a persistent cross-task retrieval memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: N/A in the retrieval sense — no top-k ranking and no minimal-set recovery objective. The whole in-context dataset (up to context length n, e.g. n=500 for basic bandits, 200 for linear bandits, H-length / cross-episode windows for MDPs) is conditioned on; the learning objective is predicting the single optimal action a* per query state via supervised classification, not selecting/ranking retrieved items.
retrieval_unit: (state, action, next-state, reward) transition tuple — i.e., a single interaction step is the atomic context element. Each tuple xi_j=(s_j,a_j,s'_j,r_j) is embedded as one token-like vector (notably DPT does NOT split s/a/s'/r into separate tokens, unlike Decision Transformer / Algorithm Distillation); the query state s_query is a separate leading element. So the retrieved/conditioning unit is a (state,reward,action) transition tuple, aggregated into a dataset/sub-trajectory.
index_source: No retrieval index. The conditioning context is constructed per task: OFFLINE it is a static sampled dataset D ~ D_test (random or expert or algorithm-generated); ONLINE it is grown at test time from the model's own episode rollouts (online/test-time-induced). Pretraining datasets B of (s_query, D, a*) triples are induced offline by sampling tasks from T_pre and generating D via random interaction / expert demos / algorithm rollouts (e.g. TS, PPO).
index_structure_topology: Flat in-context sequence (set) of transition tuples fed to a causal transformer; because dataset order is treated as exchangeable, NO positional encoding is used for the dataset elements (order-invariance is exploited; the dataset is shuffled except in linear bandits where order matters). No vector index, no graph, no hierarchy — the 'structure' is just the transformer attention over the unordered set of transition tuples plus the query token.
retriever_type: N/A / none — there is no retriever module. Selection of relevant context is done implicitly by the transformer's self-attention over the supplied in-context dataset (LLM-as-implicit-context-processor). No BM25/dense/learned retriever performs similarity search.
retriever_learning_signal: N/A for an explicit retriever. The model as a whole is trained by SUPERVISED learning (negative log-likelihood of the optimal action a*, i.e. softmax classification over discrete actions), not by similarity labels, RL, or LM-feedback. The supervision signal is the optimal-action label a* ~ pi*_tau(.|s_query); when the optimum is unknown it can come from any (possibly inefficient) minimax-optimal regret algorithm or another RL-trained agent. The emergent in-context decision policy is therefore distilled from optimal-action prediction, NOT from a learned retrieval/value policy.
query_construction: The query/key is the raw current query state s_query (offline) or the current visited state s_h (online), concatenated as a leading element v=(s_query, 0) with the in-context dataset X=(v, xi_1, ..., xi_n). In the history-dependent theoretical variant, the conditioning also includes the within-episode history xi_{h-1}=(s_{1:h-1}, a_{1:h-1}). No query decomposition, expansion, or intent extraction.
query_granularity: Step/state-level: a prediction (and thus an action choice) is produced per query state s_h at each step h, conditioned on the (fixed or grown) dataset D (and, in the history-dependent variant, the current episode's history). In bandits (H=1) this collapses to a single per-task query. So effectively step/state-level querying within a task whose context dataset is fixed (offline) or accreted across episodes (online).
when_to_retrieve: N/A in the retrieve-or-not sense. Conditioning happens every forward pass: offline the static dataset is conditioned on at each step; online the in-context dataset is grown once per episode (after each episode the full episode's interactions are appended to D) and conditioned on at every step. So it is best described as iterative/episodic context accumulation on a fixed schedule, not uncertainty-triggered or learned-router retrieval.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule (no learned trigger): online, context grows by appending each completed episode's trajectory to D; offline, the full dataset is always present. No token-confidence, attention-uncertainty, complexity classifier, reflection-token, or agent-initiated retrieval trigger. (Exploration vs exploitation emerges from sampling actions a_h ~ M_theta(.|s_h,D) online vs taking argmax offline, not from a retrieval trigger.)
reranking: None. No reranking stage over context items.
retrieved_context_refinement: None. The in-context dataset is used as-is (optionally shuffled to exploit order-invariance). No rerank/distill/compress/decompose/distractor-filtering of the conditioning context. Robustness to imperfect context is handled by training-distribution diversity, not by a refinement module.
how_retrieved_used: Training signal + prompt/context conditioning. (1) Pretraining: supervised next-optimal-action prediction conditioned on the in-context dataset — the dataset is used as model input and the optimal action as the label (a training signal turning interaction context into a posterior over optimal actions). (2) Deployment: the in-context dataset is injected into the transformer context; a single forward pass yields a distribution over actions M_theta(.|s_h,D), from which the agent takes argmax (offline) or samples (online). The context conditions decision-making without any gradient updates at test time (in-context learning).
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-act in a single forward pass rather than explicit search/planning. There is NO tree search, MCTS, or explicit planner. The transformer maps (state, in-context dataset) -> action distribution; online it interleaves act-then-append-experience across episodes. The paper shows this emergent in-context algorithm is theoretically equivalent (under a history-dependent pretraining variant and consistency assumptions) to Bayesian POSTERIOR SAMPLING (Thompson-Sampling generalization): the forward pass implicitly samples from a learned posterior over optimal actions / tasks. So 'planning' is implicit Bayesian posterior sampling realized by the network's forward pass, not an external search loop.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-action / per-step (and per-episode for context growth). Online, the model emits one action per state via a forward pass over the current context; after each episode the full trajectory is appended to D and the process repeats. No per-CoT-step or per-token interleaving of an external retriever.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw interaction tuples: each (s,a,s',r) transition is embedded (linear layer over the stacked tuple vector of dimension 2*d_S + d_A + 1) and attended over; the query state is embedded as a leading token. So the injected context is a raw trajectory / set of raw transitions (not distilled strategies, guidelines, programs, or natural-language workflows). The model's OUTPUT is a softmax distribution over optimal actions (latent posterior over actions).
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw trajectory / raw transition tuples (lowest abstraction). The conditioning units are raw (s,a,s',r) interactions of the current task, not distilled insights, state-aware guidelines, reusable workflows, or procedural skills. Abstraction (a learned posterior / surrogate task representation, e.g. an implicit linear-bandit feature map) emerges inside the network, not in the stored unit.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Distribution-diversity / coverage-based robustness baked into pretraining: in-context datasets are deliberately diversified (Dirichlet-sampled action frequencies mixed with point-mass-on-one-arm; random/expert/algorithm-generated sources) so the model is robust to test-time distribution mismatch (the paper explicitly enumerates 3 sources of mismatch: induced state distribution, T_pre vs T_test, and online self-collected prompts). Demonstrated OOD robustness: trained on Gaussian bandits but generalizes to Bernoulli rewards and to unseen noise standard deviations; generalizes to held-out goals/dynamics/action-permutations. No explicit relevance evaluator, self-reflection, distractor filtering, or retriever-aware training module.
memory_type: episodic (in-context, transient). The only 'memory' is the in-context dataset D held in the transformer context: online it is an episodic buffer grown across episodes within a single task; offline it is a fixed prompt. It is reset per task and there is NO persistent cross-task learned/parametric memory updated at test time (parameters are frozen). Not a skill-library, workflow, graph, or persistent latent memory.
write_back: Partial/online-only, within-task: in the ONLINE setting the system appends each completed episode's interactions (s1,a1,r1,...) to the in-context dataset D, i.e. it writes its own experience into the conditioning context (in-context, non-parametric). It does NOT write back into a persistent retrievable store across tasks, and there is no parameter update. Offline: no write-back. So write_back = True only in the weak sense of growing the per-task in-context buffer online.
online_growth: Yes, but only within a single deployed task/episode-sequence (online setting): D starts empty and grows as the agent interacts across episodes of the SAME task. There is NO growth of a cross-task store and NO change to model parameters; once the task ends the context is reset. Offline: the dataset is fixed (no growth).
write_back_trigger: Per-episode (online): after each completed episode the full trajectory is appended to the in-context dataset (a fixed-schedule write, on both successful and unsuccessful episodes — all collected interactions are added regardless of outcome). Offline: never. No reflective / human-validated / success-only gating; appends are unconditional.
failure_experience_usage: Both success and failure interactions are kept in the in-context dataset (online, all episode interactions are appended regardless of return; offline datasets can be random/suboptimal). Failures are not separately labeled or contrastively used — the supervision is always the OPTIMAL action, and the model learns to infer optimality even from suboptimal/random context (it can outperform the data-generating algorithm). So failure data is used implicitly as informative context, not via explicit failure-only corrective rules or success-vs-failure contrastive storage.
memory_evolution_update: Append-only (online in-context buffer grows by appending each episode's interactions; no dedup/merge/refine/forget). Parameters are never updated at test time. No mutation of stored entries.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No explicit learned retrieval policy. However, the deployed in-context decision policy IS effectively a learned (supervised-pretrained) policy that the paper proves is equivalent to Bayesian posterior sampling: action selection is governed by a learned posterior over optimal actions, not by fixed similarity top-k retrieval. So while there is no retriever-as-policy, the context-conditioned decision rule is a learned policy (emergent PS) rather than a hand-coded rule.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent, single-model setting; no sharing of memory/experience across multiple agents or heterogeneous frameworks. (Pretraining aggregates many tasks into one model, but deployment is single-agent with private per-task context.)
benchmarks: Multi-armed bandits: 5-armed Gaussian bandits (means ~ Unif[0,1], sigma=0.3); out-of-distribution Bernoulli bandits; out-of-distribution reward-shift (varying noise std 0.0/0.3/0.5); expert-biased bandits (varying expert fraction). Linear bandits (|A|=10, latent dim d=2, fixed feature map phi). MDPs: Dark Room (10x10 grid navigation, H=100, 5 actions, sparse reward; 80 train goals / 20 held-out goals), Dark Room (Three Tasks) for trajectory stitching, Dark Room (Permuted) for novel-dynamics/action-permutation generalization (20 held-out permutations), and Miniworld (25x25 RGB image-based navigation to a colored box, 4 tasks, H=50).
benchmark_family: decision-RL (bandits + MDPs / meta-RL); embodied-style gridworld + image navigation (Dark Room, Miniworld). NOT D4RL and NOT QA/web/tool/code benchmarks — these are custom meta-RL bandit/MDP environments.
baselines: Bandits: Empirical-mean (Emp), Upper Confidence Bound (UCB), Lower Confidence Bound (LCB), Thompson Sampling (TS), LinUCB and LinReg (linear-bandit, given the true feature map phi). MDPs: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO, single-task from scratch, Stable-Baselines3), Algorithm Distillation (AD, Laskin et al. 2022 — distills RL learning histories), and RL^2 (Duan et al. — recurrent online meta-RL). DPT variants compared internally: DPT, DPT-Exp (expert-biased pretraining), DPT (Rand, PPO) and DPT trained on PPO action labels.
key_metrics: Bandits — offline suboptimality (mu_{a*} - mu_{a_hat}) and online cumulative regret (sum_k mu_{a*} - mu_{a_hat_k}). MDPs — episodic return / success at reaching the goal (offline performance given random vs expert datasets; online performance / cumulative return over episodes). All reported as mean +/- standard error over 200 test tasks (bandits) or 100 offline datasets / 20 online trials (MDPs).
headline_result: Despite being trained ONLY to predict optimal actions (never to explore), DPT emergently matches classical near-optimal RL algorithms in-context with no test-time parameter updates: online it matches UCB and Thompson Sampling on bandit cumulative regret; offline it hedges like (but distinct from) LCB; on latent linear bandits DPT pretrained on Thompson-Sampling data (which ignores the linear structure) approaches LinUCB (which is given phi) and substantially beats its own data-generating source TS — i.e. DPT provably/empirically improves over the algorithm that produced its pretraining data. Theoretically, DPT (under a history-dependent pretraining variant) is exactly equivalent to Bayesian posterior sampling, yielding regret O~(C H^{3/2} S sqrt(A K)) for finite MDPs and O~(d sqrt(K)) for latent linear bandits (vs O~(sqrt(|A| K)) for the TS source).
ablations: (1) Pretraining-data source / label source: DPT trained with random in-context datasets and OPTIMAL labels generalizes best; relaxing the optimal-action requirement by using PPO-generated action labels (DPT trained on PPO labels) and/or PPO-collected datasets, DPT (Rand, PPO), gives only a slight, marginal performance loss — showing the optimal-label requirement can be relaxed. (2) Expert-bias of pretraining distribution: DPT-Exp (pretrained on expert-biased datasets) behaves like LCB at test time, whereas standard DPT behaves like TS — demonstrating the pretraining in-context-data prior controls offline conservatism (and, per Proposition 6.4, only NON-compliant expert-bias changes the learned model). (3) Structure exploitation: pretraining on linear bandits lets DPT learn an implicit surrogate for phi and explore like LinUCB even though the source data (TS) ignores structure. (4) Stitching: Dark Room (Three Tasks) shows DPT stitches expert demos of two tasks to solve an unseen third. (5) Generalization to new dynamics: Dark Room (Permuted) — recovers optimal policy offline from only 100 samples on 20 held-out permutations, snaps to near-optimal online in one episode. (6) Sensitivity (Appendix B): robust to #layers, #attention-heads (slightly worse at 8 heads due to overfitting), embedding size; performance degrades only when pretraining data is cut to 10% (10k samples).
evaluation_decoupling: No intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG) — not a retrieval system. Evaluation is decoupled instead along RL axes: intrinsic decision-quality metrics (regret, suboptimality) are reported separately from / alongside task return, and behavior is compared head-to-head with hand-designed algorithms (UCB/TS/LCB/LinUCB) whose theoretical optimality is known. Theory (regret bounds, PS-equivalence) complements empirics.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both outcome and process. Outcome: final cumulative regret / suboptimality / episodic return. Process: full online learning curves (regret vs number of interactions / episodes — measuring exploration efficiency and sample-efficiency), demonstrated exploration behavior, conservatism, stitching, and rapid adaptation (e.g. one-episode adaptation on permuted dynamics). The PS-equivalence theorem itself is a process-level characterization of the in-context algorithm's trajectory distribution.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: The central efficiency argument is computational: DPT realizes posterior sampling — which is provably sample-efficient but normally computationally intractable (posterior maintenance/sampling) — via a SINGLE transformer forward pass with NO test-time gradient updates, amortizing the cost into pretraining. Sample-efficiency is quantified via regret bounds (O~(d sqrt(K)) linear bandits; O~(C H^{3/2} S sqrt(A K)) finite MDPs) and online learning curves showing it learns faster than its data-generating algorithm. Model is small (embedding size 32, 4 layers, 4 heads; context length 500/200 for bandits, 100 for MDPs). No explicit wall-clock/latency/$ token-cost numbers reported. [uncertain] exact inference latency / FLOPs.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed context length (no adaptive selection): basic bandits context up to n=500 transition tuples, linear bandits n=200, Dark Room/Miniworld context length 100 steps; query is a single leading element. The whole available in-context dataset (up to the fixed context length) is used — there is no top-k selection, reranking, or truncation policy. Pretraining sample counts: 100k samples (basic bandit, 300 epochs), 1,000,000 (linear bandit, 200 epochs), 100k datasets for Dark Room (80k train / 20k val), 40k for Miniworld (32k/8k).
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (this is a method + theory paper, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A as a benchmark contribution. For context, environments are synthetic/procedurally generated: bandit tasks sampled from explicit reward distributions; Dark Room is a 10x10 gridworld with 100 goal positions (80 train/20 test) and a known optimal navigation policy used to generate labels; Miniworld has 4 image-based box-navigation tasks; pretraining datasets generated by random/expert/algorithm (TS, PPO) rollouts. Answer/label verifiability is exact in synthetic tasks (optimal actions computable).
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A — not case-based reasoning. If forced to map: only a weak Retrieve-analog (conditioning on the task's in-context interaction dataset) and an implicit Reuse (forward-pass inference of the optimal action from that context). No explicit Revise or persistent Retain across tasks. Flags: [Retrieve=partial, Reuse=partial, Revise=no, Retain=no].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. It is framed as meta-learning / in-context learning / Bayesian posterior sampling.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tools/APIs; not a tool-use method).
index_content_separation: N/A (no lightweight-index-then-content separation; the entire in-context dataset is loaded directly into the transformer context).
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index or integration protocol).
adaptation_mechanism: N/A in the CBR sense. The closest mechanism is in-context adaptation via a forward pass: the frozen model conditions on the (fixed offline or online-grown) interaction dataset and produces an adapted action distribution with NO gradient updates — adaptation is latent/implicit (emergent posterior sampling), not LLM-prompted case rewriting, execution-feedback revision, or RL fine-tuning at test time.
builds_on: In-context learning of LLMs (Brown et al. GPT-3); GPT-2 architecture (Radford et al.) via HuggingFace transformers; autoregressive transformers for decision-making — Decision Transformer (Chen et al. 2021) and Algorithm Distillation (Laskin et al. 2022) (which DPT explicitly differentiates from: DPT predicts optimal actions rather than distilling an RL algorithm's learning history); meta-RL / learning-to-learn (RL^2 Duan et al., Wang et al.); Bayesian posterior sampling / Thompson Sampling for RL (Thompson 1933; Osband, Russo & Van Roy 2013; Russo & Van Roy 2014) for the theoretical equivalence and regret analysis; the in-context-learning-as-Bayesian-inference view (Xie et al. 2021); MLE generalization bound (Agarwal et al. FLAMBE).
contrasts_with: Decision Transformer (return-conditioned supervised learning — provably and unboundedly sub-optimal in common cases, cannot improve over the dataset; DPT instead improves over its data-generating algorithm); Algorithm Distillation (distills a specific RL algorithm's learning trace to imitate HOW to learn, and is trained to infer a better-than-data policy but not necessarily the optimal one — AD does worse than DPT with random in-context data); RL^2 (recurrent online meta-RL with an RL objective); single-task PPO from scratch; value/policy-based offline meta-RL methods that must handle distribution shift via pessimism/regularization or extra online interaction (DPT avoids these). Also contrasts hand-designed bandit/RL algorithms (UCB/TS/LCB/LinUCB) by matching or exceeding them emergently and amortizing posterior sampling's compute.
lineage: Group F (decision/memory/RL) — in-context reinforcement learning lineage. Sits between Algorithm Distillation (Laskin et al. 2022, distillation-of-RL-algorithm in-context RL) and later in-context-RL / sequence-model-RL work; pioneers the 'predict-the-optimal-action via supervised pretraining' route to emergent in-context RL and ties it to Bayesian posterior sampling theory. Within the survey's retrieval lens it represents the extreme where the 'retrieved context' is the agent's own in-context interaction dataset (episodic, non-parametric, no external corpus or similarity search), contrasting with classic RAG planners that retrieve from a static external corpus and with experience/case-memory agents that maintain a persistent growing store.
